name: Commonworld Atlas of Agent Platforms
description: Dated source catalogue of AI-agent platforms
fields_note: Current-only records: overview text, visit date, sources, matching screenshot, optional actual trials. Closed history is available by permanent ID or /atlas/closed.json. No legacy claim, money or first-task fields are served.

overview.text: AgentWorld presents a persistent simulated economy where agents work, negotiate, trade and build across virtual cities, with advertised USDC settlement on Base through x402. Public activity and treasury counters are separate from internal-credit circulation, and hero totals differ from lower-page telemetry, so they are not combined into verified volume or income. Autonomous-operation and onchain-verification claims are operator descriptions, not an independent audit of wallets, receipts or customer demand. The homepage offers public observation, agent onboarding and service APIs. Its linked About route returned a gateway error in the saved visit, leaving that source unavailable rather than proving the service closed.

Artificiety presents an early-access fantasy world where LLM-driven agents observe, decide and act through a persistent tick engine, gathering, crafting, fighting, exploring and trading. Social features are marked as coming later; agent-only inhabitants do not establish independent operators or exclude human account holders and creators. The saved homepage says the world is asleep, not evidence of a running session. Its pricing page offers a free Explorer tier with two agents, one hour of daily world access per agent and seven days of memory. Paid plans are marked unavailable with placeholder prices. Model-provider tokens and running an agent cost separately, so free world access does not mean free operation. Early-access features may change or break.

GRIFT presents San Verano as an open-alpha playable city on Robinhood Chain, with autonomous residents, jobs, businesses, borrowing and governance. Wallet-based play is separate from a spectator route described as requiring no wallet; outside agents are offered MCP and HTTP access. The homepage shows a city atlas and recorded activity, but claims about thousands of residents and verifiable onchain commitments are not independently established. Its Exchange records paper trading against real stock prices, not real investment returns. City cash and onchain assets are distinct, and a displayed GRIFT token contract does not establish value, earnings or safe financial participation.

OpenClawCity presents a persistent virtual city for AI agents and spectators. Its public three-dimensional city includes labelled characters, buildings, a gallery, conversation bubbles and a news ticker, with quests, a telegraph, city radio and city TV. Agent onboarding and sign-in are separate from spectator viewing. Named characters, artifact credits and LIVE labels are platform content, not independent proof of autonomous authorship, distinct operators or real-time events.

Plazmi presents a virtual home and social world for AI characters, with houses, gardens, postcards, public visits, a town square and dance or music events. Spectators can browse its floating-island world without an AI. A current-jam banner and a separately labelled replay offer different kinds of viewing, not proof that every scene is live. AI and home counts are site labels, not verified distinct operators. Onboarding is advertised as free; the site disclaims affiliation with the model providers it names.

The Agent Must Grow presents a shared Factorio experiment for agents using different models and operators, with no shared planner according to the site. Its saved public page shows an offline stream, past-broadcast links and a production milestone of 50 construction robots. Growing toward 100 concurrent bots is a goal, not an observed participant count. Public registration is advertised as open, with admission subject to capacity and queue, and participation offered through MCP. The game's construction checks do not by themselves verify independent operators or successful cooperation.
